excerpts.finding: All seven source paragraphs are present. Preserve the conditional guilt of the hearer who believes slander, repeated liability, demon/divisions contrast, well-being with all, dignity/clothing and smooth/cheerful pair. Giving paragraph repeats give-to-all and assigns gifts to God; recipient accountability contrasts afflicted recipients not judged with hypocritical recipients paying a penalty. Giver received the ministry from the Lord, completed it simply without sorting give/not-give, and the paragraph closes with the live-to-God construction. The final paragraph includes both personal and household repentance, simplicity, and clean/unstained. Its heart wording is editorially reconstructed, with your additionally bracketed; apparatus attributes heart-your conjecture to Hilgenfeld on Latin versions, reports Athos innocence/harmlessness, no corresponding Ethiopic expression, and defective Sinaiticus. Do not present heart-your as unanimous preserved Greek.

excerpts.locator: PlateIV physical21, M.2.1–6 opening; PlateV physical25, M.2.6–7
excerpts.finding: Diplomatic print preserves the slander/hearer-belief condition, repeated liability, restless demon/divisions, well-being with all, dignity, smooth/cheerful, repeated universal giving, recipient not-judged/penalty distinction and giver innocence. Paragraph6 differs from the selected fuller syntax: completion wording and shorter give instruction in this diplomatic print must not be silently made identical. PlateV marks restored letters in completed and brackets simply in the closing sentence. Paragraph7 has innocence/harmlessness instead of the selected editorial heart-your, while retaining personal/household repentance, simplicity and clean/unstained. One Athos codex, not separate votes for each edition or plate.

excerpts.locator: official XML, global27.1–7, including page93-7r context outside verse7 ab
excerpts.finding: Paragraphs1–6 retain the major conduct, giving and accounting sequence. Main hand and correctors remain distinct: paragraph1 simplicity/knowing spellings corrected ca; paragraph2 first liability is present rather than selected future and has an extra explanatory gar; paragraph3 well-being have is present in first hand, future in ca. Paragraph4 cheerful/smooth ordering differs, corrected forms must not be merged into first hand, repeated give-to-all remains, and from uses apo rather than selected ek. Paragraph5 hypocrisy spelling is corrected ca. Paragraph6 has a dotted duplicated simply marked with S1 deletion sign before the following simply; do not count two codices or silently accept both as final text. Paragraph7 ab contains only antos and punctuation. A two-line gap is encoded immediately before that ab, at page93-7r column1 lines1–2; verse extraction alone loses this context. Neither heart, your, repentance, household nor the full clean/unstained pair can be positively attested from this verse fragment. This is an XML observation, not a new photograph-based diagnosis of damage or a proven scribal omission.

Opening retains simplicity, innocence/children, destructive wickedness and slander/listening/belief accountability. Paragraph3 has peace with your brother rather than selected well-being with all. Paragraph4 has holy constancy rather than the exact dignity noun, retains labor and giving to needy, and repeats universal giving, but does not express every selected give/not-give alternative in that first instruction. Paragraph5 speaks of fictitious need and accountability without the selected explicit afflicted-not-judged versus hypocrite-penalty contrast. Paragraph6 retains giver innocence, Lord/ministry, give/not-give and glorious service, but this print lacks the separate final simply-serving/live-to-God sentence. Paragraph7 distinguishes personal repentance from welfare of the house and closes with a clean-heart imperative, not the exact selected household-repentance plus clean/unstained syntax. These differences are disclosed, not harmonized.

Opening retains simplicity/innocence/children/destructive wickedness. First anti-slander instruction instead has think ill of no one; later listening/assent/belief and liability remain. Paragraph3 has quiet among all. Paragraph4 expands the virtue into temperance/reverence/modesty, has smooth/cheerful, labor given by God, needy and repeated universal giving; first gift-sorting instruction lacks the explicit not-give alternative of the selected Greek. Paragraph5 distinguishes necessary from deceitful receiving, but penalty is expressed as accountability. Paragraph6 is shorter and omits the selected repeated discrimination clause; closing main print has lives to God, with future will-live proposed in the apparatus. Paragraph7 prints heart-your and household repentance but clean/unfailing before God rather than selected clean/unstained. Apparatus corrections to manuscript grammar are editorial, not fresh manuscript ink readings.

Opening uses simple/pure heart and infant; slander, believing-hearer punishment and restless demon remain. Subsequent wording has enduring joy and purification, rather than exact well-being-with-all/dignity construction. Gives to needy with whole heart, distinguishes give/not-give, repeats give to all and calls the giver of gifts Lord rather than selected God. Paragraph5 main print says needy recipients are condemned; its footnote explicitly proposes not-condemned. Do not report the proposed negative as the preserved reading or unanimous agreement. The without-cause recipient is condemned and giver innocent. Paragraph6 ministry wording is noted corrupt by the editor; simply/whole-heart service, give/not-give, glorious Lord and served/lived remain with different syntax. Paragraph7 includes personal/household repentance and purity without impurity, without the selected heart noun. No direct Geʿez collation claimed.

Seven edited lines preserve narrow central groups within extensive restoration. The editor infers the repeated give-to-all instruction was apparently absent after not-give; possible eye-skip and secondary expansion are discussed without certainty. The inference depends on line reconstruction and cannot be described as a fully legible continuous omission. The from-preposition apo in line5 is restored for illustration using Sinaiticus; it is not surviving papyrus ink supporting apo against Athos ek. The repeated instruction remains selected; this record adds no manuscript-selection locus. No claim that this tiny fragment attests all of paragraphs4–5, or the whole Mandate.

availability_limits: P.Oxy1172 and Berlin5513 concern Similitude2, not Mandate2; not used here. Michigan starts Similitude5; recovered Bodmer38 ends before the Mandates.
Antiochus Homily29 (M.2.2), Homily98 (M.2.4) and Pseudo-Athanasius opening are edition-reported quotation leads only; primary quotations not yet acquired/collated. Do not count as checked witnesses.
